text:
Kai: heads-up — since the GPU pool autoscale at ~11:05 UTC we've had intermittent 502/503s hitting the edge inference path. Looks correlated with pods coming up on new nodes, ~50-90s after node ready. Anyone seen similar with headless services + node-local-dns?
Dennis: saw that too, noticed client-side retries drop to different pod IPs but some DNS A records still point to old IPs for a minute. possible node-local-dns caching.
Sasha: which service is this? the stateful headless for model-workers or the fronting nodeport service?
Kai: model-workers is headless (clusterIP: None) for direct discovery. Front LB is a separate NodePort that routes to a kube-proxy rule we use for canary. Failures are coming when requests from the LB hit nodes where kube-proxy thinks pod IPs are not endpoints yet.
Maria: ok interesting. can you paste the EndpointSlice and node-local-dns pod logs from a node that exhibited the problem?
Kai: pasted snippets below from node gpu-edge-11 (timestamps match the scale event)

----- kubectl get endpointslice -n edge model-workers -o yaml (trimmed) -----
- metadata:
    name: model-workers-abcde
  endpoints:
  - addresses:
    - 10.240.5.12
    conditions:
      ready: true
  - addresses:
    - 10.240.8.3
    conditions:
      ready: false
-----

----- dig +short model-workers.edge.svc.cluster.local @10.96.0.10 -----
10.240.5.12
10.240.8.3

----- journalctl -u node-local-dns.service (excerpt) -----
Mar 12 11:06:12 node-local-dns[1234]: Cache miss for model-workers.edge.svc.cluster.local
Mar 12 11:06:13 node-local-dns[1234]: Cached reply for model-workers.edge.svc.cluster.local -> 10.240.5.12
Mar 12 11:06:40 node-local-dns[1234]: Ignoring endpoint 10.240.8.3 -> marked NotReady by endpointslice

Dennis: if endpointslice shows NotReady for new pod IPs the LB -> node path can still route to them if kube-proxy has stale iptables/ipvs rules. kube-proxy sync timing vs endpointslice readiness matters.
Sasha: seeing logs from kube-proxy on that node?
Kai: kube-proxy shows repeated "Failed to update proxy rules: endpoint not found" around the same window. then a sync succeeds ~70s later.

----- kube-proxy log -----
W Mar 12 11:06:05 kube-proxy: sync failed for svc model-workers: endpoint not found
I Mar 12 11:07:20 kube-proxy: successfully updated rules for svc model-workers

Maria: ok, hypothesis: endpoint controller marks endpoint notReady while the pod init/sidecar hasn't finished readiness probe; node-local-dns caches the old IP set or the NotReady IP depending on sequence; kube-proxy had intermediate state where rules missing which causes NodePort/LB hit to drop packets.
Julia: related note — we ran into a similar pattern when conntrack timeouts + kube-proxy sync race created sticky failures for ephemeral pods. Could be amplified by autoscale and new AZ nodes.
Kai: nodes are same AZ but GPU provisioning spun up taint/toleration cycle. timeline: node added -> kubelet registers -> pods scheduled -> pod network up -> readiness probe late -> endpointslice toggles -> kube-proxy sync lag -> node-local-dns stale answers -> LB hits wrong node.
Dennis: actionable — short term: (1) restart node-local-dns on affected nodes to clear cache (2) bump kube-proxy syncPeriod lower for edge pool to reduce lag (3) ensure readinessProbe includes the sidecar network init so endpoints are only marked ready once reachable
Sasha: also add a temporary nginx ingress annotation to fallback to 502->retry on different backend instead of returning 503, buys time for sync.
Maria: can we instrument endpoint controller latency? also check apiserver watch conn drops, that sometimes causes endpoint slice controller to lag.
Kai: I ran `kubectl get events -n kube-system --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod` and saw watch reconnects around the same time.

infra-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-1180 — "edge-node-local-dns + endpoint slice sync race causing transient 5xx". Assigned to eng-infra.

Julia: long term: we should
- add readiness gating for model-worker sidecars so endpoint readiness aligns with actual traffic path
- consider enabling endpointSlice TTL or reducing caching TTL at node-local-dns if feasible
- move critical LB path to externalTrafficPolicy=Local with controller aware of endpoints to avoid proxy races
- investigate switching kube-proxy to ipvs mode for faster rule convergence on large scale events

Kai: short term actions I'll take now:
- restart node-local-dns pods on the 3 affected nodes (done)
- open PR to lower kube-proxy syncPeriod in edge pool for next deploy
- add readiness probe tweak to model-worker chart and rollout to staging

Dennis: +1 on PR review, will monitor metrics and trace rates. I'll also add a Grafana alert for EndpointSlice creation latency > 20s.
Sasha: thanks — please paste final runbook steps in the incident ticket so on-call can follow.

Kai: will do. marking this thread for follow-up after the kube-proxy sync change is deployed. :white_check_mark:
